# 2.15.0

The last of the audit list. Two behaviour changes on the published surface, both of them the
code finally doing what it was already written to do, and one deletion.

## Behaviour changes — read these

- **The global `JSON.stringify` replacement is gone.** Importing `core/common` used to install a
  process-wide reimplementation of the builtin, so every consumer of this package *and every
  third-party library loaded beside it* serialised through it. It existed for one reason: a
  `CObjectID` must travel as its value rather than as `{"value":1}`. `CObjectID` now declares
  `toJSON`, which the engine calls before the replacer exactly as the old wrapper did, so that
  behaviour is unchanged — and the builtin is the real one again.

  Three divergences from the specification disappear with it. An **array replacer is a property
  allow-list that the spec applies to object properties only**; the replacement applied it to
  array indices too, so `JSON.stringify({a:[1,2,3]}, ['a'])` came back as `{"a":[null,null,null]}`.
  Output key order followed the object instead of the replacer, so `{b:1,a:2}` with `['a','b']`
  serialised as `{"b":1,"a":2}`. And a caller's replacer function was invoked without its holder,
  so `this` was never the enclosing array — the only way a replacer can tell an element from a
  property.

  Anything that breaks here was relying on one of those three, i.e. on corruption.

- **`bars.tickSize` derives a value again instead of reporting 0.** `CBarsBase.tickSize` is meant
  to fall back to the greatest common divisor of the closes when the caller gave no tick size.
  The getter read `this._ticksize ??= gcd(closes)` while the constructor stores `tickSize ? tickSize : 0`
  — always a number, never nullish — so the fallback never ran. Zero is this class's
  invalid-cache marker, not "unset": `CBarsMutableBase` carries a `_tickSizeAuto` flag whose only
  purpose is to reset `_ticksize` to 0 on every mutation, the line that does it says
  "new/updated bar changes closes -> reset tickSize cache", and the sibling getter
  `CQuotesHistory.tickSize` already uses the falsy check. One token, `??=` to `||=`, and the
  fallback, the three cache resets and the flag all mean something again.

  **This one can reach existing code.** A caller that reads `if (bars.tickSize)` as "was a tick
  size supplied?" now sees a derived value where it used to see 0. The raw cache is unchanged and
  still readable as `bars._tickSize`. `CBarsInternal` in `MarketData` overrides the getter
  outright and keeps its deliberate `?? 0`.

## Removed

- **`src/Common/rcp/oldCommonsServer.ts`** (671 lines) — a file of `@deprecated` forwarders onto
  `oldCommonsServerMini`, with zero importers anywhere in the repository and no entrypoint
  declaration re-exporting it; the package `exports` map has no wildcard for `lib/Common/*`, so no
  consumer on the supported Node range could reach it either. The live names it forwarded to —
  `promiseServer`, `wsWrapper`, `createClientProxy`, `createAPIFacadeServer` — are unaffected, and
  `oldCommonsServerMini` itself stays (`createRpcServerAutoDetect` uses it).
- **`src/Common/events/Listen3.ts`** — a two-line compatibility shim for old *internal* deep
  imports, referenced by nothing.

Deliberately NOT removed after checking the published surface: `createRpcClientAuto` (zero internal
callers, but exported from three entrypoints and documented with an example in `rpc.md`) and the
`listenSocketAll` / `listenSocketSmart` pair (runtime bodies are identical, but both names are
public and `listen-deep` builds its public types on both `ReturnType`s; collapsing them saves eight
lines and risks the type surface).

## Documented, not changed

- **`Date.prototype` is patched process-wide** by importing the root, `./client` or `./server` —
  subpath entrypoints such as `./rpc` and `./observe` never reach `Time` and leave `Date` alone.
  `toJSON`, `JSON.stringify` and `valueOf` are untouched. The patched `toString` parses back
  through `new Date()` to second precision in whole-hour zones only; in fractional-offset zones
  (UTC+5:30, +5:45) it yields `Invalid Date`. Nothing in the library round-trips a date through
  `toString`, so this is a note for consumers, not a defect.
- **`objectSet` does not filter path segments** — `__proto__` as an intermediate segment writes
  onto `Object.prototype`. It has no internal callers and sits outside the RPC boundary, which has
  its own `isSafeKey`-guarded resolver, so no wire path reaches it. Noted in the rare docs rather
  than guarded, because a guard here would cost every caller and protect none of them.
- **`tInfoForLoadHistory.right` is not implemented.** The chunker anchors at the newest edge and
  steps backwards while the dispatch loop only starts a load where the chunk list descends, so
  `right: true` resolves to `[]` without ever calling `funcLoad`. Nothing in the repository passes
  it and there is no recorded contract for what it should do; implementing it means a mirrored
  forward chunker, which is feature work rather than a fix. The type now says so.

Proof, not assertion: `oracle/regression/json-stringify-fidelity.spec.ts` checks the patched global
against a `JSON.stringify` taken from a fresh V8 realm — for every input free of `CObjectID` the two
must agree byte for byte and produce the same replacer calls with the same holders. It fails on the
previous code in three of seven cases. `oracle/regression/bars-ticksize.spec.ts` fails in two of
five. 120/120 oracles green.
